newsitem.title: YEMEN: Yemen coalition party warns of polls court action.
newsitem.headline: Yemen coalition party warns of polls court action.

text.p: The junior partner in Yemen's coalition government on Wednesday accused election supervisors of bias, threatening court action over results of the country's first poll since a 1994 civil war.

The Islah Party -- influential Islamists ruling with President Ali Abdullah Saleh's General Peoples Congress (GPC) -- said early results from the Supreme Election Committee for Sunday's poll were false.
The committee said on Tuesday the GPC had won more than two-thirds of initial votes counted. Final results are due on Thursday.

"The Supreme Elections Committee is known to have been biased in favour of one party since the first stage of the elections," Islah's Secretary General Mohammad al-Yadomi said in apparent reference to the GPC.
Tuesday's results, he said, were "incorrect" and aimed at "misleading domestic and external public opinion."
He said his party would go to court over the alleged bias.
"If the judicial system will not be fair, we will give the seats we won to the GPC," he said. "We will withdraw from the election process without any regrets."
As tension between the ruling parties rose, a security official said four people died in armed clashes between GPC and Islah backers.
Tuesday's initial results showed the GPC had won 93 constituencies, Islah 16 and independents 24. Other parties had won two in the 301-seat parliament.
Yadomi ruled out violence as a response to the alleged irregularities, amid continuing reports of election-related clashes.

The security official said the GPC-Islah clashes which resulted in four deaths, in Hajja 130 km (80 miles) northwest of Sanaa, followed a dispute as ballot boxes were being transferred to the capital.
"On their way, they (the two sides) stopped to pray and tensions rose again and they began exchanging fire."

In separate incidents, an election worker died when supporters of independent candidates exchanged fire, while elsewhere an independent candidate died when a soldier hurled a hand-grenade into the courtyard of a polling station following tension among candidates and supporters, the security official said.

The attacks raised the number of deaths in poll-related violence to at least 20, but officials have played down the incidents labelling the attacks criminal. Election observers noted Yemenis often carry weapons.
Islah said on Wednesday its calculations at 11.00 a.m. (0800 GMT) showed the GPC had won 130 of 207 districts counted, Islah 41, independents 33 and other parties three.
In united Yemen's first elections in 1993, the GPC won 123 seats, Islah 62 and the Yemen Socialist Party 56. Independents won 47 while the rest went to Baathist and Nasserite parties.
